gaps.sentence: The village ___ a lot since the new road opened.
gaps.hint: since clause with a present result
gaps.explanation: Change that started in the past and continues to now takes the present perfect: has changed.

gaps.sentence: We ___ each other since primary school, so nothing surprises me about him.
gaps.hint: since primary school continuing to now
gaps.explanation: A state continuing since a past point takes the present perfect: have known.

gaps.sentence: Who ___ this bag belong to? It has been sitting here all morning.
gaps.hint: the question form needs auxiliary does
gaps.explanation: Present simple questions need the auxiliary 'does' plus the base verb: does this bag belong to.

gaps.sentence: Don't wake him — he has just ___ asleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Has just' is followed by the past participle: fallen.

gaps.sentence: I ___ here for two years, so I know the system well.
gaps.hint: for two years continuing until now
gaps.explanation: 'For two years' with present relevance takes the present perfect, often continuous: have been working.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys again — this is the third time this month!
gaps.hint: third time this month connects to now
gaps.explanation: 'This is the third time' links a recent event to now, so the present perfect is required: has lost.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the car tonight, so take a taxi into town.
gaps.hint: a future activity in progress as reason
gaps.explanation: The future continuous can express something in progress around a future time, here as a polite reason: will be using.
